errors.wrong_site_type: This is not possible for this type of site.

check.nameFormat: Use 2 to 32 characters: lowercase letters, digits, _ and -, starting with a letter.
check.domainsMax: A site can have at most {{count}} domains.
check.domainParts: "{{domain}}" needs at least two parts, like example.com.
check.domainChars: "{{domain}}" is not a domain. Use letters, digits and inner hyphens; write other characters in their xn-- form.
check.domainIp: "{{domain}}" is not a domain. IP addresses are not allowed.

pool.label: {{name}} ({{path}})
pool.unmounted: The volume of this pool is not mounted. Sites cannot be created there until it is.
pool.noQuota: This pool has no disk quota: sites on it get no disk limit.
pool.counting: Disk limits on this pool are not enforced. See Health.

change.phpStops: The PHP {{version}} pool stops. The PHP settings and the page cache stay stored for a switch back.
change.keepsPort: The new one keeps its port.
change.venvStays: The environment .venv stays in the home.
change.proxyStops: nginx no longer passes requests to {{target}}.
change.accountStarts: A Linux account with its home is created in the pool {{pool}}, with the default limits.
change.staticStarts: nginx serves the files of {{dir}} as they are, without PHP.
change.phpStarts: A PHP {{version}} pool starts and serves the site's PHP files.
change.nodeStarts: The Node.js {{version}} app starts on its own port.
change.nodeWaits: The Node.js app gets its own port. It starts once its start command is set.
change.appStarts: The program {{program}} starts on its own port.
change.appWaits: The app gets its own port. It starts once its program is set.
change.pythonStarts: Hostashi creates the environment .venv with Python {{version}} if the home has none, and the app gets its own port. It starts once its start command is set and its packages are installed.
change.redirectStarts: nginx sends every address to {{target}} with status {{status}}.
change.domainsStay: The domains, HTTPS and the certificate.
change.accountStays: The Linux account with its files, databases, cron jobs, SSH logins, backups and limits.
change.accountKept: The Linux account with its files, databases, cron jobs, SSH logins and backups. You can remove them afterwards on the overview.

list.title: Sites
list.description: Every site has its domains and certificate. PHP, static, Node.js and app sites also have their own Linux user; redirect and reverse proxy sites have none.

create.title: New site
create.description: A site answers for its domains: with PHP, static files, a Node.js app or a program of its own from its own Linux user and home, or as a redirect or reverse proxy.
create.applicationHintDir: Serves the {{dir}} folder and brings the hardening rules for {{profile}}; both can be changed later.
create.applicationHint: Brings fitting hardening rules; they can be changed later under Security.
create.noPhp: No PHP version is installed. Install one under PHP, or create a static site.
create.parked: {{domain}} is parked. Its parking page ends when the site is live.
create.name: Name
create.nameHintWeb: The name of the site in the panel. 2 to 32 characters: lowercase letters, digits, _ and -.
create.nameHint: Becomes the Linux user of the site. 2 to 32 characters: lowercase letters, digits, _ and -.
create.displayNameHint: Shown in the panel instead of the name. Free text, up to 64 characters; it can be changed at any time.
create.domainsHint: One per line. The first one is the primary domain.
create.poolHint: Where the site's home lives. A site stays on its pool.
create.legacy: PHP {{version}} gets no or only security fixes upstream. Use it only for software that needs it.
create.onlyInstalled: Only installed versions are listed. Install more PHP versions
create.staticHint: The web root folder, a fallback for single-page apps and asset caching can be set on the site's Web tab.
create.tls: HTTPS with a Let's Encrypt certificate
create.hsts: HSTS: browsers use only HTTPS for this site
create.tlsHint: The domains must point to this server, or the certificate cannot be issued.

choice.php: WordPress, Laravel, TYPO3 and other PHP software.
choice.static: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, for example the build of Hugo, Astro or a single-page app. No PHP.
choice.node: An app such as Next.js, Nuxt or Express that runs all the time as the site's user. Requests go to its port.
choice.python: A Django, Flask or FastAPI app that runs all the time as the site's user, from its own environment .venv. Requests go to its port.
choice.app: A program of your own, for example a Go or Rust service, that runs all the time as the site's user. Requests go to its port.
choice.proxy: Passes every request to another web server, for example an app in your network. No files, no Linux account.
choice.redirect: Sends every address to another one, for example an old domain to the new one. No files, no Linux account.

page.systemNameTip: Linux user, home folder and SSH login
page.openTip: Open the site in a new tab
page.certFailed: The certificate could not be issued
page.certFailedText: Last attempt failed: {{error}}. Hostashi tries again within an hour.
page.readOnlyStaff: An administrator or manager changes these settings.

details.title: Details
details.label: Details of {{site}}
details.accountNote: (Linux user, home folder and SSH login)
details.disabled: Disabled: everybody gets the chosen maintenance page
details.disabledPhp: Disabled: everybody gets the chosen maintenance page, PHP is stopped
details.disabledApp: Disabled: everybody gets the chosen maintenance page, the app is stopped
details.maintenance: Maintenance: visitors get the maintenance page
details.maintenanceExcept: Maintenance: visitors get the maintenance page, except {{ips}}

rename.title: Rename
rename.shownAs: The site is now shown as {{title}}.
rename.label: Display name
rename.hintAccount: Shown in the panel instead of the system name, up to {{max}} characters. The system name {{name}} stays: Linux user, home folder, SSH login and API keep it.
rename.hint: Shown in the panel instead of the system name, up to {{max}} characters. The system name {{name}} stays in the API.

availability.title: Availability
availability.disabledText: The site is disabled: visitors get the page below with “503 Service Unavailable”. Enabling it serves its files and starts PHP again.
availability.confirmText: Visitors get the chosen maintenance page with “503 Service Unavailable” and PHP stops. There are no allowed addresses. Files, databases, backups and the certificate stay. You can enable the site again at any time.
availability.hint: A disabled site shows a maintenance page to everybody.
availability.hintPhp: A disabled site shows a maintenance page to everybody and its PHP is stopped.
availability.hintApp: A disabled site shows a maintenance page to everybody and its app is stopped.

delete.title: Delete site
delete.hintAccount: Deletes the site with its files and its databases. Backups stay until they expire.
delete.hintProxy: Deletes the site and its reverse proxy. It has no files or databases.
delete.hintRedirect: Deletes the site and its redirect. It has no files or databases.
delete.parkHint: To keep the domains answering, delete the site and park its domains in one step.
delete.leftOut: Domains you leave out are free afterwards.
delete.tls: HTTPS with a Let's Encrypt certificate
delete.confirmHint: The site is deleted with its files and its databases. This cannot be undone.

httpsTab.title: HTTPS
httpsTab.off: HTTPS is off. The site is served over HTTP.
httpsTab.onWaiting: HTTPS is on. The site switches when its certificate is there.
httpsTab.hstsOn: HSTS is on. Browsers keep using HTTPS for this site, even if HTTPS is turned off later.
httpsTab.tlsHintReadOnly: An administrator or manager turns HTTPS on or off.
httpsTab.letsEncrypt: HTTPS with a Let's Encrypt certificate
httpsTab.hstsHint: Turning it on asks first: browsers remember it for a year.
httpsTab.hsts: HSTS: browsers use only HTTPS for this site
httpsTab.askOffText: The site is then served over plain HTTP: passwords and cookies travel unencrypted. Browsers that know HSTS for it refuse to open it.
httpsTab.askHstsText: Browsers that visit the site remember for a year to use only HTTPS, even if HTTPS is turned off here later. Turn it on once the certificate works for every domain of the site.
httpsTab.hstsOnlyHttps: HSTS is sent only while the site is served over HTTPS.

phpTab.title: PHP version
phpTab.runsOn: The site runs on PHP {{version}} now.
phpTab.off: PHP is off for this site now.
phpTab.programsOn: PHP of this site may start programs now.
phpTab.programsOff: PHP of this site can no longer start programs.
phpTab.label: PHP of {{site}}
phpTab.onlyInstalled: Only installed versions are listed. <php>Install more PHP versions</php>. To turn PHP off, make it a static site on the <web>Web</web> tab.
phpTab.programsReadOnly: An administrator or manager changes this.
phpTab.programsHint: Off by default: a hacked plugin then cannot run commands on the server. Turn it on only for software that needs it, for example image optimizers or PDF tools. WP-CLI, Composer and cron jobs are not affected.
phpTab.programsSwitch: Allow PHP to start programs (exec, system, shell_exec, proc_open, popen)

maintenance.off: Maintenance is off. Everybody sees the site again.
maintenance.onListed: Maintenance is on. The listed addresses still see the site.
maintenance.on: Maintenance is on. Every visitor gets the maintenance page.
maintenance.noIp: Your address is not known to the panel.
maintenance.hintOn: On: visitors get the page with “503 Service Unavailable”.
maintenance.hintOff: Visitors get the page with “503 Service Unavailable”; the allowed addresses still see the site.
maintenance.disabledWins: The site is disabled. Disabled wins: everybody gets the page chosen under Availability until it is enabled.
maintenance.allowedHint: IPv4 or IPv6 addresses or ranges like 10.0.0.0/8, one per line, at most 20.

tiles.title: Status
tiles.label: Status of {{site}}
tiles.included: The last run included this site

typeCard.title: Site type
typeCard.noPhp: No PHP version is installed. Install one under PHP first.
typeCard.keepsAccount: Another type keeps the Linux account, files and databases; only what serves the site changes.
typeCard.createsAccount: A type with files creates a Linux account for the site.

account.title: Linux account
account.left: This site still has a Linux account and files
account.leftProxy: They are left from its former type and keep working: SSH and SFTP, cron jobs and backups. nginx serves only the reverse proxy.
account.leftRedirect: They are left from its former type and keep working: SSH and SFTP, cron jobs and backups. nginx serves only the redirect.
account.user: the Linux user {{site}} and its home with all files
account.databases: the site's databases and their users
account.rest: its cron jobs, SSH keys, limits and object cache
account.staysProxy: The reverse proxy, the domains and HTTPS stay. Backups stay until they expire.
account.staysRedirect: The redirect, the domains and HTTPS stay. Backups stay until they expire.

clone.title: Copy this site
clone.intro: Creates a new site with a copy of the files, the databases on this server and the settings. A staging copy is for trying changes: its cron jobs are paused, it asks for a password, search engines are asked not to index it, and it can be refreshed from this site later.
clone.name: System name of the copy
clone.nameHint: Linux user and home folder of the new site.
clone.domainHint: Point it to this server first, so the copy gets its certificate.
clone.mailWarning: The copy takes over the application's own mail settings and can send real mail.
clone.mailWarningText: Environment variables of the app are copied too and may hold live API keys. Databases on external database servers are not copied: the copy keeps using them.
clone.copyFailed: Copying is not possible here. Select the password and copy it by hand.
clone.saveTitle: Save the password of the copy now
clone.saveText: The copy {{site}} is being made and asks every visitor for this login. Hostashi does not keep the password and cannot show it again; you can set a new one under Security, Access.
clone.deletedSource: a site that was deleted since
clone.beforeTestText: The application's own mail settings were copied, so the copy can send real mail. Environment variables of the app may hold live API keys.
clone.unknownConfig: Hostashi does not know this application's configuration. Change it by hand:
clone.dbConnection: The database connection: use <dbs/> instead of the source's databases. The new passwords are set under Databases.
clone.ownAddressSource: The site's own address: {{domain}} instead of the source's domain, in the configuration and in the database.
clone.liveServices: Mail, payment and other live services, so tests do not reach real customers.
clone.maintenanceHint: Visitors see the maintenance page until the files and databases are copied, so nothing changes on the site halfway through the copy.
clone.refreshHint: The files and databases of {{site}} are replaced with those of {{source}}. Changes made on the copy are lost. Domain, password and users stay.

errors.clone_running: A copy of this site is running. Wait until it is done.
errors.clone_unavailable: Copying sites is not available on this panel.
errors.not_a_clone: This site is no staging copy of an existing site.

cutover.label: DNS switch of {{site}}
cutover.intro: When the files and databases are in place, point the domains of {{site}} at this server. The panel checks the domains every minute and turns HTTPS on once all of them point here.
cutover.setRecords: Set these records for every domain below at your DNS provider and remove all other A and AAAA records:
cutover.noServer: This server's public addresses are not known yet.
cutover.now: What the domains resolve to now:
cutover.firstCheck: The first check runs in a moment.
cutover.longTtl: Some records are cached for more than 5 minutes.
cutover.longTtlText: Lower their TTL to 300 seconds and wait for the old TTL to pass before you change the addresses, so that visitors switch over quickly.

wordpress.running: WordPress is being installed. This takes about a minute.
wordpress.occupied: The document root holds files, but no WordPress.
wordpress.occupiedText: WordPress installs only into an empty folder. Reinstall replaces the files with a new WordPress.
wordpress.reinstallTitle: Reinstall replaces the site with a new WordPress.
wordpress.reinstallText: Everything in the document root is deleted: themes, plugins, uploads and any other files.
wordpress.reinstallDb: The database {{database}} is deleted as well.
wordpress.reinstallBackup: Back up the site first under Backups; this cannot be undone.
wordpress.intro: Installs the latest WordPress into the empty document root, with a new database and user for it. WP-CLI runs as the site user; file editing in the dashboard stays off.
wordpress.adminUserHint: Not admin, which bots try first.
wordpress.generate: Generate a strong admin password (shown once)
wordpress.discourage: Discourage search engines in WordPress (Settings, Reading)
wordpress.copyFailed: Copying is not possible here. Select the password and copy it by hand.
wordpress.saveTitle: Save the WordPress admin password now
wordpress.saveText: Hostashi does not keep it and cannot show it again. If it is lost, reset it from the WordPress login page.

errors.wordpress_unavailable: The WordPress install is not available on this server.
errors.not_found: The site does not exist anymore.
errors.notEmpty: The document root is not empty. WordPress installs only into an empty folder.
errors.generic: The WordPress install could not be started or read. Try again.
